comparisons.reason: Different constructs. Feature 0 is positive when a comment cites a concrete, identifiable real-world example (event, case, person, organization, place, study, historical instance, or a statistic from a real source). Feature 1 is positive when a comment contains specific numerical data or statistics. A named historical case with no figures gives 1 for feature 0 and 0 for feature 1. A comment with specific numbers and no identifiable real source gives the reverse. Feature 0 counts only identifiable real-world examples and excludes hypotheticals. Feature 1 counts quantitative figures whether or not they come from an identifiable source. The two features share only the OC_comments source, the binary dtype, and the 0 and null handling.
